<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD is safe for the narrow gate of `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` and `makepkg --printsrcinfo`.

The `source` array fetches two files from the project's own upstream (y3owk1n/neru on GitHub): the release zip binary and the LICENSE file. This is standard packaging practice. The binary archive has a pinned sha256 checksum, while the LICENSE source is SKIP — both are acceptable per the gate criteria.

The top-level scope of the PKGBUILD contains only variable assignments. There is no `pkgver()` function defined, so no code executes there. There is no `prepare()` function. The `package()` function contains standard `install` operations and uses the installed binary to generate shell completions, but this function will not execute during `--nobuild --noprepare`.

No dangerous top-level commands, no obfuscated code, no network exfiltration, no unexpected downloads, and no evidence of supply-chain attack vectors that would trigger during the source-fetch and PKGBUILD-parse steps.
</details>
<evidence>
